simple.meaning: שַׁחַר (shachar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “dawn (literal, figurative or adverbial).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 25 times in Genesis, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, Nehemiah, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 19:15. The surrounding contexts include family line, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁחַר (H7837) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שַׁחַר (shachar) / H7837 is traced through Genesis 19:15, Genesis 32:25, Genesis 32:27, Joshua 6:15 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.usage: day(-spring), early, light, morning, whence riseth.
definitions.full: H7837. shachar שַׁ֫חַר noun masculine Gen 19:15 dawn ; — absolute ׳שׁ 1Sam 9:26 +, שָׁ֑חַר Judg 19:25 +; suffix שַׁחְרָךְ Isa 47:11 (but read probably שַׁחֲדָהּ ); — dawn , with עָלָה rise Gen 19:15 ; 32:25 , 27 ; Josh 6:15 (all J), Judg 19:25 ; 1Sam 9:26 ; Neh 4:15 ; Jonah 4:7 ; opposed to עֵיפָה Amos 4:13 ; as adverb at dawn Psa 57:9 = 108:3 ; ׳עַפְעַמֵּישֿׁ Job 3:9 ; 41:10 ; ׳כַּנְפֵישֿׁ Psa 139:9 ; 110:3 read probably שׁ ׳רֶחֶם (see מִשְׁחָר below); ׳שׁ also Job 38:12 , in simile Hosea 6:3 (but read נִמְצָאֵהוּ כֵּן כְּשַׁחֲרֵנוּ as infinitive, see following, Gie Beitr. 208 We Now GASm Marti), Isa 58:8 ; Song 6:10 ; Joel 2:2 (al. blackness , || וַעֲרָפֶל עָנָן ); ׳בֶּןשֿׁ Isa 14:12 (of star, figurative of royal splendour; — literal as myth RS K 300 ); שׁ לוֺ ׳אֵין 8:20 is obscure, so also ׳בַּשּׁ Hosea 10:15 (We in storm , i.e. בַּשַּׂעַר ). — Isa 47:11 usually, but improbably, dawn (origin) of calamity: JHMich Hi Ew Rö (Thes) De Di and others charm away (RVm) (Arabic enchant (We Heid. 2. 159, 200 ), enchantment [= Sabean סחר DHM Hofmus. 24. 1 ]); but see [ שָׁחַד ].
